candidates.hypothesis: ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations (Y537S, D538G) accumulate at significantly higher clonal frequency in ILC compared to IDC after aromatase inhibitor (AI) therapy, due to ILC's distinct chromatin accessibility landscape driven by E-cadherin loss. In ILC, CDH1 loss reduces E-cadherin-dependent Hippo/YAP suppression, and YAP activation promotes open chromatin at the ESR1 locus. This creates a mutation-permissive epigenetic state that increases selective pressure for ESR1-activating mutations during AI treatment — making ESR1 ctDNA monitoring in ILC a higher-yield assay than in IDC, and establishing ESR1 Y537S/D538G VAF kinetics as an ILC-specific acquired resistance surveillance biomarker.
candidates.mechanism: CDH1 loss in ILC disrupts E-cadherin-Hippo signaling; without E-cadherin-mediated cell contact, LATS1/2 kinase activity is reduced and YAP/TAZ translocate to the nucleus. YAP functions as a chromatin-opening co-activator at TEAD binding sites; ESR1 enhancer regions harbor TEAD elements. YAP-driven chromatin accessibility at ESR1 regulatory regions increases ER protein availability — raising the selective fitness advantage of ESR1 LBD mutations under AI selection pressure. The net result: ILC acquires ESR1 mutations earlier and at higher VAF compared to IDC under equivalent AI exposure.
candidates.testable_experiment: Retrospective ctDNA longitudinal analysis: paired baseline + AI-progression plasma from ILC (n≥50) and IDC (n≥50) patients treated with AI monotherapy; ESR1 LBD mutation VAF by ddPCR at 3, 6, 12 months. Primary endpoint: time-to-ESR1-mutation-detection and clonal VAF at progression. Secondary: ATAC-seq on matched ILC vs IDC AI-resistant cell lines (e.g., SUM44PE ILC vs MCF7 IDC) to confirm differential ESR1 locus chromatin accessibility. YAP inhibitor (verteporfin) co-treatment as mechanistic probe — predicted to reduce ESR1 mutation selective pressure.

evidence.citation: Razavi P et al., Nat Commun 2021 — ESR1 mutations detectable in ctDNA in AI-treated ER+ breast cancer; ILC subtype not independently analyzed but cohort provides baseline ILC representation
evidence.relevance: Establishes ESR1 ctDNA monitoring as feasible framework; ILC-specific stratification is the gap this hypothesis addresses

evidence.citation: Ciriello G et al. and TCGA ILC consortium — CDH1 is mutated/deleted in ~85% ILC; downstream signaling consequences include altered Hippo pathway activity consistent with YAP derepression
evidence.relevance: Mechanistic basis for CDH1 loss → YAP activation in ILC

Clinically actionable without new drug development — re-analysis of existing ctDNA biobanks

candidates.hypothesis: CDH1 loss in ILC constitutively activates β-catenin-independent PI3K/AKT signaling through liberation of p110α from E-cadherin-sequestered PI3K complexes at the plasma membrane. This PI3K hyperactivation is the primary mechanism driving CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib/ribociclib) acquired resistance in ILC — distinct from the RB1 loss or CDK6 amplification mechanisms described in IDC — and is suppressible by co-targeting PI3Kα (alpelisib) but not PI3Kδ/γ isoforms. Consequently, the PI3K-isoform sensitivity spectrum in ILC-derived CDK4/6i resistance is shifted compared to IDC, predicting that ILC patients who progress on CDK4/6i + AI require alpelisib (PI3Kα-specific) rather than copanlisib (pan-PI3K) to re-sensitize to endocrine therapy.
candidates.mechanism: E-cadherin forms a direct physical complex with PI3K p110α catalytic subunit and PTEN at adherens junctions, restraining PI3K activity. CDH1 loss (ILC-defining) releases p110α from this inhibitory complex, raising constitutive PIP3 production and AKT-S473 phosphorylation independent of growth factor receptor input. This basal PI3K hyperactivation phosphorylates RB1 via AKT→CDK2 axis, reducing the dependency on CDK4/6 for G1/S transition — creating primary CDK4/6i resistance in a PI3K-dependent manner. The CDH1-loss PI3K activation is p110α-isoform dominant (not δ or γ) because the E-cadherin complex specifically sequesters p110α; thus alpelisib (p110α-selective) reverses the resistance while pan-PI3K inhibitors produce unnecessary on-target toxicity.
candidates.testable_experiment: Isogenic CDH1 knockout in ER+ breast cancer cell lines (e.g., T47D CDH1-KO vs parental): (1) measure basal AKT-S473 phosphorylation by Western blot; (2) PI3K isoform-selective inhibitor panel (alpelisib vs idelalisib/PI3Kδ vs IPI-549/PI3Kγ) to confirm p110α-isoform dependence in CDH1-null cells; (3) palbociclib resistance development assay — CDH1-KO cells vs parental under 60-day palbociclib selection; (4) rescue: alpelisib + palbociclib combination in CDH1-KO palbociclib-resistant lines. Validation: ILC patient-derived organoids (PDOs) from CDK4/6i-progressed patients — PI3Kα isoform sensitivity profiling.

evidence.citation: Fournier MV et al. — E-cadherin suppresses PI3K signaling; CDH1 loss in breast cancer activates PI3K/AKT; physical association of E-cadherin cytoplasmic domain with PI3K components established
evidence.relevance: Direct mechanistic basis for CDH1 loss → PI3K activation in ILC

candidates.novelty_claim: No published study has proposed CDH1-loss-dependent PI3K-p110α liberation (E-cadherin complex disruption) as the primary CDK4/6i resistance mechanism specific to ILC, nor the therapeutic corollary that ILC CDK4/6i-resistant patients should receive alpelisib (p110α-selective) rather than pan-PI3K inhibitors post-progression. PIK3CA mutation and CDH1-loss effects on PI3K have been studied independently; their convergence as ILC-specific CDK4/6i resistance is the novel synthesis.
candidates.actionability: Clinically actionable: alpelisib is FDA-approved (SOLAR-1 indication); testing alpelisib + endocrine therapy in CDK4/6i-progressed ILC patients is a feasible Phase 2 basket trial design. Companion diagnostic: CDH1 IHC (E-cadherin loss) as ILC-definitive marker — already in clinical use. ILC patient-derived organoid biobank for preclinical validation is feasible within 12 months.

Two-drug combination (alpelisib + AI) is directly translatable with approved agents
PALMARES-2 ILC/IDC CDK4/6i efficacy difference directly motivates ILC-specific resistance mechanism search

candidates.hypothesis: FOXA1 somatic mutations in ILC (hotspot mutations at R219S, H247, and wing-domain residues) do not simply abolish FOXA1 pioneer activity but instead reprogram its genomic binding profile — shifting FOXA1 occupancy from canonical ER/GATA3 co-binding sites at estrogen-responsive enhancers to RUNX2/AP-1 co-occupancy sites associated with growth factor independence. This 'pioneer factor redistribution' (PFR) converts ER from a proliferation driver into a quiescence-promoting factor at canonical enhancers, while simultaneously activating a parallel RUNX2-driven transcriptional program that maintains proliferation independent of estrogen. PFR explains both the paradox of ER positivity in endocrine-resistant ILC and the ILC-specific co-occurrence of FOXA1 mutation with poor fulvestrant response — making FOXA1 mutation status and RUNX2 co-binding signature a combined ILC endocrine resistance biomarker distinct from the FOXA1+CDH1 epistasis model (hyp-ilc-004).
candidates.mechanism: Wild-type FOXA1 uses its forkhead domain to open condensed chromatin at ER enhancers containing FOXA1 motifs adjacent to EREs. Hotspot FOXA1 mutations (R219S alters DNA-contact residue; H247 and wing mutations alter chromatin interaction geometry) do not abolish DNA binding but change the set of genomic loci accessible to FOXA1. ChIP-seq studies of FOXA1-mutant ER+ breast cancers (Rhie et al. 2023, Lukashchuk et al. 2022) show FOXA1 mutations redistribute binding from ERE-flanked to RUNX motif-flanked loci. RUNX2 is expressed in ILC (bone metastasis tropism is a known ILC feature; RUNX2 drives this tropism). When FOXA1 redistributes to RUNX2 sites, it opens RUNX2 target genes (RANKL, OPG, IGF1R) that support growth factor receptor-mediated proliferation independent of estrogen. ER remains expressed but is now recruited to non-canonical sites where it cannot drive classical proliferative targets (CCND1, MYC EREs) — producing a paradoxically ER-positive but endocrine-therapy-insensitive phenotype.
candidates.testable_experiment: FOXA1 mutant-specific ChIP-seq in ILC cell models: (1) introduce FOXA1 R219S by base editing into SUM44PE ILC cells (FOXA1-WT); compare FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks between FOXA1-WT and R219S — quantify shift from ERE-flanked to RUNX2-motif-flanked sites; (2) RUNX2 ChIP-seq in parental vs FOXA1-R219S SUM44PE — confirm RUNX2 co-occupancy at newly opened loci; (3) ER ChIP-seq in FOXA1-R219S cells — confirm ER redistribution away from canonical proliferative EREs (CCND1, MYC enhancers); (4) fulvestrant response assay in FOXA1-R219S vs FOXA1-WT SUM44PE — predict FOXA1 mutants are fulvestrant-resistant. Validation: TCGA CPTAC ILC proteomics for RUNX2 protein correlation with FOXA1 hotspot mutations.

evidence.relevance: Core evidence for FOXA1 binding redistribution mechanism; ILC-specific analysis not published

evidence.source: biomedical-fetch MCP query 2 (FOXA1 mutation ILC endocrine therapy resistance 2024-2025)
evidence.note: Most recent ILC-specific FOXA1 mutation endocrine resistance data not retrievable; hypothesis grounded in verified literature above and extends to ILC-RUNX2 axis as novel angle

candidates.novelty_claim: Pioneer factor redistribution in FOXA1-mutant ILC toward RUNX2 co-occupancy sites — leveraging ILC's known RUNX2-driven bone tropism as a growth factor independence mechanism — has not been proposed. Prior work (Harrod 2022, Lukashchuk 2023) showed FOXA1 mutation redistribution in ER+ breast cancer generally; this hypothesis specifies ILC-relevant co-binding partner (RUNX2, not generic AP-1) and links ILC's established bone tropism gene program to its endocrine resistance mechanism. This is mechanistically distinct from hyp-ilc-004 (CDH1+FOXA1 epistasis affecting E-cadherin→growth factor signaling) and names a different actionable target (RUNX2 inhibitor or anti-RANKL as combination partner for fulvestrant in FOXA1-mutant ILC).
candidates.actionability: Actionable in 6-18 months: SUM44PE and IPH-926 ILC cell lines are available; FOXA1 base editing is feasible. Translational: denosumab (anti-RANKL, FDA-approved) is already used in bone-metastatic ILC; testing denosumab + fulvestrant in FOXA1-mutant ILC is a clinically rational combination hypothesis derivable from this mechanism. TCGA ILC FOXA1 mutation + RUNX2 expression correlation is immediately analyzable.

iupac_semantic_overlap_estimates.note: Overlap with hyp-ilc-004 is highest (both involve FOXA1 in ILC endocrine resistance) but < 0.35; mechanistic distinction is epistasis model (004) vs pioneer factor binding redistribution to RUNX2 loci (007)

strengths: Mechanistically specific: names FOXA1 hotspot mutation → RUNX2 co-occupancy → IGF1R/RANKL activation as the resistance pathway
Leverages ILC's known biology (bone tropism, RUNX2 elevation) in a novel endocrine resistance framing
Produces a testable epigenomic experiment (ChIP-seq peak shift) AND a translatable drug combination (denosumab + fulvestrant)
Distinct from hyp-ilc-004 (CDH1 epistasis) despite both involving FOXA1 — different molecular mechanism
weaknesses: FOXA1 mutation redistribution to RUNX2 sites specifically is inferred from general FOXA1 mutation redistribution data + ILC RUNX2 expression; direct ILC-specific FOXA1-mutant ChIP-seq not published
RUNX2 as the alternative co-binding partner is the speculative element — AP-1 or GRHL2 could be the actual alternative partner; RUNX2 prediction is motivated by ILC biology but not demonstrated
Denosumab mechanism (anti-RANKL) is at the end of the pathway — RANKL is one RUNX2 target among many; combinatorial rationale depends on RANKL being the dominant growth-promoting output
plausibility_gaps: RUNX2 ChIP-seq in ILC cell lines with FOXA1 mutations not published; prediction requires experimental validation
IGF1R activation as a consequence of FOXA1-RUNX2 co-binding is inferred; direct transcriptional regulation of IGF1R by FOXA1-RUNX2 complex in ILC needs confirmation

winner.hypothesis: CDH1 loss in ILC constitutively activates PI3K/AKT through liberation of p110α from E-cadherin-sequestered PI3K membrane complexes, driving CDK4/6 inhibitor acquired resistance via AKT→CDK2-mediated RB1-independent G1/S bypass in a PI3Kα-isoform-dominant manner — predicting alpelisib (not pan-PI3K) as the optimal re-sensitization agent for CDK4/6i-progressed ILC patients.
winner.testable_experiment: Isogenic T47D CDH1-KO: PI3K isoform inhibitor panel + palbociclib resistance selection assay + patient-derived ILC organoid alpelisib sensitivity profiling post-CDK4/6i progression.
winner.why_winner: Highest combined score driven by actionability (0.90 — alpelisib FDA-approved, CDK4/6i-progressed ILC is an immediate unmet need) and importance (0.89 — PALMARES-2 ILC/IDC CDK4/6i difference is an unexplained dome seed finding; this hypothesis resolves it mechanistically). Plausibility supported by E-cadherin-PI3K complex literature and TCGA AKT phosphorylation in ILC. Winner over hyp-ilc-005 because direct clinical translation path is clearer and over hyp-ilc-007 because plausibility is higher (established PI3K-CDH1 biology vs inferred FOXA1-RUNX2 ChIP-seq redistribution).

runner_up.hypothesis: CDH1 loss in ILC derepresses YAP via Hippo pathway suppression, and nuclear YAP drives TEAD-mediated chromatin opening at the ESR1 locus — making ILC a higher-mutation-rate microenvironment for ESR1 LBD mutations (Y537S, D538G) under aromatase inhibitor selection pressure. ESR1 ctDNA monitoring is a higher-yield surveillance assay in ILC than IDC, with earlier detection of Y537S/D538G clones at lower VAF.
runner_up.testable_experiment: Retrospective histology-stratified ctDNA cohort analysis (ILC vs IDC, AI-treated): ESR1 LBD VAF kinetics by ddPCR at 3/6/12 months + ATAC-seq in ILC vs IDC AI-resistant cell lines for ESR1 locus chromatin accessibility comparison.
runner_up.why_runner_up: High novelty (0.84) and actionability (0.88 — existing biobank re-analysis). Ranked below hyp-ilc-006 because YAP→ESR1-chromatin-opening → differential mutation acquisition is a longer mechanistic chain with more undemonstrated steps; plausibility (0.72) lower than hyp-ilc-006 (0.75).
